## Research question

How has the share of the population living in extreme poverty changed over time in Jamaica, Canada, the United States, India, Brazil, Spain, Nigeria and South Africa?

## Background

Extreme poverty is one indicator of material deprivation. Comparing countries over time can help researchers examine differences in poverty trends, while recognising that a single international poverty threshold does not capture every dimension of poverty.

## Data and methods

The data come from [Our World in Data](https://ourworldindata.org/grapher/share-of-population-in-extreme-poverty), using a measure based on the World Bank's international extreme-poverty threshold of \$3 per day.

The analysis covers available observations from 1990 onwards. Countries do not have the same number of observations, and some years are missing. Lines between observed values should therefore be interpreted with caution.

## Results

````         

```{r}
#| label: fig-poverty-trends
#| echo: false
#| message: false
#| warning: false
#| fig-cap: "Extreme poverty trends across eight countries. Source: Our World in Data, based on World Bank data."

library(readr)
library(dplyr)
library(ggplot2)

poverty_url <- paste0(
  "https://ourworldindata.org/grapher/",
  "share-of-population-in-extreme-poverty.csv",
  "?v=1&csvType=full&useColumnShortNames=false"
)

poverty_data <- read_csv(
  poverty_url,
  show_col_types = FALSE
)

countries_to_compare <- c(
  "Jamaica", "Canada", "United States", "India",
  "Brazil", "Spain", "Nigeria", "South Africa"
)

poverty_countries <- poverty_data |>
  filter(
    Year >= 1990,
    !is.na(`Share of population in poverty ($3 a day)`),
    Entity %in% countries_to_compare
  ) |>
  arrange(Entity, Year)

poverty_plot <- ggplot(
  poverty_countries,
  aes(
    x = Year,
    y = `Share of population in poverty ($3 a day)`,
    colour = Entity,
    group = Entity
  )
) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 0.8, na.rm = TRUE) +
  geom_point(size = 1.8) +
  labs(
    title = "Extreme poverty across eight countries",
    subtitle = "Share of the population living on less than $3 per day",
    x = "Year",
    y = "Population in extreme poverty (%)",
    colour = "Country",
    caption = paste(
      "Source: Our World in Data, based on World Bank data.",
      "Observations are not available for every country in every year."
    )
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 12) +
  theme(
    legend.position = "bottom",
    plot.title = element_text(face = "bold"),
    legend.title = element_text(face = "bold")
  )

poverty_plot
```
````

## Discussion

## Limitations

- The international extreme-poverty measure does not capture all dimensions of poverty.

- Data availability differs between countries and years.

- The chart is descriptive and does not establish the causes of changes in poverty.

## Conclusion

Summarise the main patterns, explain why they matter, and identify one question for further research.
